"Zionism is the vast, enormous, unbelievably successful rescue project." So
[claimed](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=chuJEHv6LQU) the Zionist activist
Haviv Rettig Gur in a Tuesday interview with the 'Breakfast Club' show.

"Zionism is a rescue project" has long been a key Zionist talking point. Even
if Zionism has meant displacement, apartheid, and genocide for the
Palestinians, at least it meant heroic rescue for Jews, right?

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Wrong. Zionism was not about rescuing Jews; it was about establishing a
"Jewish state" in an overwhelmingly non-Jewish country. Those two goals were
frequently at odds, which is why Zionist doctrine was hostile to persecuted
Jews for decades. They were deemed a material and spiritual burden. Zionist
leaders wanted "pioneers," meaning young, wealthy, and healthy Jews, not
families, refugees, or invalids. Persecuted Jews were themselves persecuted by
Zionism.

But it gets worse. Persecuted Jews were not just a financial burden and a
moral stain, but efforts to rescue them were considered existential threats.
The idea that Jews could be saved anywhere other than Palestine, so Zionist
logic went, undermined the whole idea of Zionism. This is why Zionist leaders
sabotaged countless rescue efforts. The movement staked its claim to
legitimacy on rescuing Jews, as Rettig Gur reminds us, while Zionist leaders
constantly intervened to prevent the rescue of Jews. It was one of the most
cynical, if successful, narrative coups in history.
